items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: one of the boys, Gene Cedric -- he was tenor saxophone

ctx.x: drive down Unter den Linden. And then the others went to Tier Park and then we went into the Tier Gardens, and there was a place there called Krohl Garden, which fascinated us. The Germans had these big bands playing there in these prestige coffee-houses. Sometimes something like 25 men playing in these coffee-houses. Which we don't have today. But in those days it was really a life that we didn't know and Berlin was such a beautiful place that, really, those days there, we really enjoyed.

Now we was all staying at -- we lived at a place called Darmstader Hoff. This all happened in East Berlin, on Friederich-strasse. And as we were standing outside talking, one of the boys, Gene Cedric -- he was tenor saxophone, later on became very popular over here with Fats Waller and some other -- anyhow, he was reading a letter from St. Louis. And it was telling him about -- so the guys all gathered around him and said, 'Gee, you got a letter.' So this old German woman come up too, and she stood right there…
were specialists in those days, they were not generalists.
